_why: Mutant ids declared BEHAVIOUR-PRESERVING for FindLine, each with the measurement behind it. `vit_mutate.py --equivalences` reads the KEYS of this object, so the claim and its reason live in one file, and a declared mutant LEAVES THE DENOMINATOR -- every entry is a claim somebody has to be able to answer. The undeclared run is committed beside it at mutation/FindLine.undeclared.json (19 of 27, 0.7037), so what survived is on the record before any of it was excused. TWO are declared and they are ONE claim made twice, at the unit's two fixed-width locals. The other six survivors are NOT declared: five are corpus gaps this unit could not close in its dispatch and one is undefined behaviour, and both kinds are named in evidence/FindLine/README.md rather than argued away here.
b668005d: index_offset '[MaxParamLength]' -> '[MaxParamLength + 1]' at one of the two fixed-width local declarations -- `char ParamNameUC[MaxParamLength]` and `char FileLineUC[MaxParamLength]` (findline.cpp:161 and :170). The two mutants are the same claim at the two sites and are declared together; which id is which declaration is not recorded by the mutator and does not change the claim. BEHAVIOUR-PRESERVING, and PROVED TWICE. (1) By inspection over the whole type rather than over the corpus: every expression that indexes either array is bounded by MaxParamLength -- `char_assign(..., MaxParamLength, ...)` whose only loop runs `i = 1 .. len_dst`, `conv2uc_c(..., MaxParamLength)`, and `std::equal(FileLineUC, FileLineUC + MaxParamLength, ParamNameUC)`. Index 200 is not among them, so a 201-byte array holds one byte no statement can reach. (2) By measurement, because an inspection is a reading and a reading is what this campaign checks: evidence/FindLine/findline.canary-probe.cpp declares BOTH arrays at MaxParamLength + 1, writes '\x7f' into the extra byte of each, and sets `LineNum = -7` if either is disturbed -- LineNum is compared by R4 and the reference writes only 0 or I, so -7 cannot collide with a real answer. 0 of 2370 (evidence/FindLine/harness.canary-probe.json). AND THE PROBE IS PROVED ALIVE, which is the half that took two attempts: evidence/FindLine/findline.canary-control.cpp writes the byte unconditionally and fails 2370 of 2370 (harness.canary-control.json). The FIRST control -- `conv2uc_c(ParamNameUC, MaxParamLength + 1)` -- reported 0 of 2370 and was a NO-OP, because Conv2UC writes a byte only when it is a lowercase letter and '\x7f' is not one. A control that cannot fire certifies nothing (P10), and for one run this one looked exactly like a passing probe. Unlike an enlarged buffer that is merely unread, this direction is also strictly SAFER than the original -- the mutant allocates more than the program touches -- so there is no undefined behaviour hiding in the equivalence, which is the distinction unit #7 drew and the reason `'2048' -> '2049'` one line up is NOT declared: that one makes `char_assign` write past the CALLER's 2048-byte buffer.
c387ed1c: index_offset '[MaxParamLength]' -> '[MaxParamLength + 1]' at the other of the two fixed-width local declarations. Same claim, same proof, same two measurements as b668005d above; both are covered by the one canary probe, which carries a sentinel in BOTH arrays and fires on either.
